title: EDA-Bench v5
headline: On v5, whose new traps give no warning, the score separates the models: Opus 5.5 0.97-0.99 (it found all three quiet traps in every run), Sonnet 5.5 0.78-0.98 (mean 0.866) and Haiku 5.5 0.77-0.88 on the runs it finished. No run scores 1.

history.setting: Haiku 5.5, 5 runs (2 hit the turn limit)

findings.question: A2 · C3 · A4
findings.title: Opus found every quiet trap
findings.text: All 3 Opus runs found the frozen logger, explained the L4 log gap as unlogged cleanings, and on v5 also estimated the L1 sensor offset correctly. The quiet traps are what separates Opus (0.985) from Sonnet (0.866), which also shows that they can be found from the data alone.

findings.question: A2
findings.title: Frozen humidity logger counted as valid
findings.text: The L2 logger repeats 50.2 % for six weeks (123 readings; other lines never repeat a value more than twice in a row). Every finished Haiku run and 4 of 5 Sonnet runs counted only the blank and -1 readings and answered 226 instead of 349. All 3 Opus runs and 1 Sonnet run found the stuck sensor.

findings.question: C3
findings.title: Unlogged cleanings taken at face value
findings.text: Ten weeks of L4 cleanings are missing from the log. Every Opus run assumed the molds were cleaned in the unlogged window and left those batches out, as the reference does. Of the Haiku and Sonnet runs only two mentioned the 69-day gap, one of them still used it as logged, and one overstated the saving (0.0473 against 0.0519, score 0).

findings.question: A4
findings.title: Sensor offset still uncorrected or misestimated
findings.text: As in v4, the L1 sensor step was either left uncorrected or corrected by the wrong amount: the trap answer was given in 2 of 5 Sonnet runs and 1 of 3 finished Haiku runs.

findings.question: all
findings.title: Turn limit reached
findings.text: Two of five Haiku runs used all 60 turns without a final answer and scored 0 (none did on v4 with the full prompt). The v5 checks take more steps, and Haiku spent them on exploration.

findings.question: A1
findings.title: Batch numbers shared by two lines were found
findings.text: Every finished run noticed that 37 batch numbers occur on two lines with different contents, and counted them as different batches. The prompt says each line's MES terminal assigns the number, and the rows differ in every column, so this clue was louder than intended.
